title: UNKNOWN Entity reference by case variation — targetEntity 'WIDGET' is well-formed but matches no declared entity
why: The manifest declares 'Widget' and the Action targets 'WIDGET'. The reference is grammatically valid — '^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$' accepts an all-caps name — but no entity by that exact name is declared, so it resolves to nothing and must fail closed exactly like az7-n2. This fixture exists because the tempting repair for az7-n2 is a case-insensitive lookup, and a case-insensitive lookup is itself a vulnerability: it lets an App name a target that is not the entity it declared, and combined with az7-n5a it lets a same-name-different-case decoy supply an ownership relation the real target does not have. Reference resolution must be exact and case-sensitive.
notes: VALIDATOR OBLIGATION, NOT A SCHEMA ONE. Like az7-n2, deciding this requires joining action.targetEntity against the sibling entities[].name values, which draft 2020-12 cannot express. The schema will and should ACCEPT this document — 'WIDGET' is a valid $defs/entityName. DO NOT REPORT THAT ACCEPT AS A SCHEMA FAILURE. This is a negative-control fixture for the resolution algorithm rather than for the grammar.
